chapter: Joe Oliver and the second line
title: The second line and funeral parade customs
summary: Armstrong explains the second line in parades, pool hall followers and the grand marshal, and is asked about bands meeting in the street.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, you said you played second line to Joe. What do you mean by... It's a trumpet. Oh, the harmony part. The second line is in the parade.

What's that? The guys who like to do art fellas, they got on uniforms. Yeah. And they're to parade. Well, you know there's like the pool hall gang. Oh, the guys that, uh, who could drive a car for any chance, but he's got time to follow the parade. Well, they can't get in the parade. So they'd be on the other side of the city. And then join them, and they're just the same as one of the members. Yeah. And when the grand marshal stands, he stands up at a corner. Now these guys over there, marching with him, doing the band. So they'd be waiting to see which way he's going to turn it. And he'd go out to the shop. So if he'd turn that way, he'd come catch him in the house. And he'd go over the water across the other side of the street. And then, uh, if he'd march in and turn this way, then everybody would run right through the parade. I'd get over there. And I'd get over there.

In the temple. Skip it, you know. What would happen if he had two funerals the same day and the bands met out in the street? Would you have a battle? A jam session? Well, if he don't turn the coffin over there, I mean.
